name: Regionalism (politics)
summary: Regionalism seeks more political power and self-determination for people in a subnational region, from devolution and autonomy to full independence. Adherents argue that decisions closer to the people allow locally tailored policy, better resource allocation and protection of regional language and culture. It is a territorial doctrine with no fixed economic programme, and regionalist parties range from the left to the conservative.
scope: Regionalism as a political position: consciousness of and loyalty to a distinct region, and the development of a political or social system based on regions (Merriam-Webster), in particular the demand of territorially concentrated communities for self-government within or beyond the state, and the 'new regionalism' of Western Europe in which state competences shift up to Europe and down to regions (Keating). Regionalist parties are the parties that campaign on it, a subset of regional parties, and Raos shows them spread across several European party families, so their economic and social positions vary. Excludes regional parties with no demand for autonomy, and the linguistic/literary senses of the word.

sources.title: Between Autonomy and Secession: Decentralization and Regionalist Party Ideological Radicalism (Massetti and Schakel, Party Politics 2016; accepted manuscript, Wayback copy of the University of Trento repository)
sources.author: Emanuele Massetti and Arjan H. Schakel
sources.usedFor: Regionalist parties, autonomy versus secession, their ideology beyond the region-state dimension.

notes: Themes searched: definition, scope, self-determination, secession, autonomy, language and minority rights, European integration, civic versus ethnic nationalism. Only three defining sources name regionalism (Merriam-Webster, Keating 2004, Raos 2011); the SEP federalism entry and the EFA 2019 manifesto never name it and were dropped as coatracks. They describe movements and parties, and regionalist parties range from left to conservative, so economic and social statements are null. Massetti and Schakel 2016 was read through a Wayback copy of the repository's accepted manuscript.
